title: rollup-ladder-latency-budgets-and-dash-skeleton
summary: Working notes proposing a compact rollup ladder, per-level latency budgets, and a reusable investigation dashboard skeleton tailored to tokenized LLM inference.
motivation: High-level latency alerts are noisy and slow down diagnosis. We need a small, opinionated set of rollup levels and quantile budgets so on-call can narrow scope quickly (global -> tenant -> route -> session -> raw-token).
definitions: raw-token: single emitted token span with full tags; session: a user interaction/request seen as one logical inference invocation; route: API surface (ex: /v1/chat/completions); tenant: customer namespace; trace-anchor: stable id used to jump from metric point to trace (request_id preferred).
dashboard_guidelines:
Dashboard skeleton for an investigation page:
- Header: active alerts, time selector, last-deployed commit id.
- Row A (quick triage): global p99 latency sparkline, total QPS, pct of requests with kv_cache_hit.
- Row B (rollup ladder): five small panels stacked left-to-right showing same quantile across global -> tenant -> route -> session -> raw-token with baseline overlays. Each panel has a consistent color/quantile and a jump-to-trace button.
- Row C (supporting): batch size distribution, GPU utilization, queue depth, error rate.
- Row D (heatmaps): sequence-length heatmap and p95 by seq-length bucket.
- Instrumentation footer: owner, estimated cardinality, expected query cost, linked PR/Jira.
Rules: one investigation dashboard per SLO class; avoid mixing cost metrics with latency-focused pages.
tracing_anchors:
Primary anchor: request_id. Fallback anchor: tenant_id + rounded_ts + route + prefix_hash.
For fanout: include parent_request_id and fanout_index on child spans.
Sampler rule: retain 100% of traces that fired an alert tag for 10 minutes, otherwise sample raw-token traces at 1% and session traces at 5% to control retention.
Add metric_rollup_level tag on spans that correspond to an alerted metric to ease trace queries.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (2w): audit current metrics to confirm available dims and owners.
Phase 1 (4w): implement ingestion rollup mapping and dimension trimming with unit tests and cardinality guards.
Phase 2 (2w): ship dashboard templates and jump-to-trace plumbing.
Phase 3 (2w): pilot on one high-traffic route, gather SRE feedback and tune budgets.
Phase 4 (2w): wide rollout + migration playbook and cost estimation.
open_questions:
- What exact cardinality caps can infra guarantee for raw-token dims per minute?
- Should raw-token series be downsampled to 1Hz after 24h to control DB cost?
- Are we willing to enforce model aliasing to limit tag length/cardinality?
- How to handle cross-tenant global alerts without spamming tenants?
notes_to_self: Next actions: schedule sync with SRE + Serving Runtime, raise instrumentation gaps in jira:OBS-4827, draft example dashboard JSON for pilot route and attach query cost estimate to github issue.
